variants.headline: Accident at a workplace
variants.sub: The workplace {facility} has had an accident.
variants.body:
An accident has occurred at {facility}. The occurrence is established, while a particular injury or legal finding is not supplied here. Readers considering {target} should distinguish scrutiny of safety responsibility from an invented account of the accident's cause or the condition of those involved.

Going to work should not make a person's safety an afterthought. Labour has every reason to insist on that principle. We should also distinguish an accident from an unreported finding about its cause, because solidarity requires a truthful account as well as a firm demand for decent conditions.

The role of {target} merits scrutiny against the accident. This paper does not presume a breach of rules or announce consequences for workers that have not been established in the reported particulars. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.

variants.headline: Workplace safety becomes immediate news
variants.sub: There has been an accident at {facility}.
variants.body:
The workplace {facility} has had an accident. A workplace accident has occurred in the colony. An assessment of {target} should take that event seriously without presuming the kind of work, the number affected or a breach of rules not established by this account.

variants.headline: An accident enters the working day
variants.body:
There has been an accident at {facility}. That is sufficient reason for careful attention, not permission to imagine an injury or a rescue. For {target}, the relevant question is responsibility in the setting of work, with the known event kept distinct from its unreported particulars.
